speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start with the mechanism of injury: can you describe exactly what happened during the rear-end collision and how your leg was positioned when the pain started? Please rate your pain on a scale of 1 to 10.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the right groin pain and abnormal positioning, do you feel any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your right leg or foot? Also, can you try to straighten your right leg without lifting your heel off the bed?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation.

The classic presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg following trauma is highly specific for this injury. I am requesting an AP Pelvis X-Ray to confirm the femoral head position within the acetabulum. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvis_XRay
